  SUBJECT: CSE 3122/CSE_3122 - SOFTWARE ENGINEERING  
  SOFTWARE ENGINEERING [CSE 3122]  
  Marks: 50                                                                              Duration: 180 mins.  
  A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1A)          Using an example, explain the evolution of software development methodologies over  
  the past six decades. Include a graph to support your explanation.                         (2)  
  
  1B)          With the help of a diagram describe the working of the Exploratory style of software  
  development                                                                                (3)  
  
  1C)          Describe ANY FIVE shortcomings of the Iterative waterfall model  
  (5)  
  
  2A)          Explain all the basic activities that Extreme Programming(XP) prescribes to be part of  
  the software development process.                                                          (5)  
  
  2B)          Identify two main functional requirements of Railway Reservation System in the correct  
  format.                                                                                (3)  
  
  2C)          Explain the terms decision table and decision tree. Organize the decision tree given in  
  Figure. 1 into an equivalent decision table.  
  
  
  (2)

  3B)   A software development company is tasked with designing an online library  
  management system. They have created a module that handles book lending, user  
  management, and report generation in the same module. Analyse the cohesion level of        (3)  
  this module and recommend a design change to improve cohesion, explaining how this  
  change would enhance the system's design.  
  
  3C)   For the given case study generate DFDs for level 0, 1 and 2. Also, provide the data  
  dictionary.  
  
  A supermarket aims to implement an automated system for a customer loyalty scheme  
  designed to reward regular customers. The system will handle customer registration,  
  purchase tracking, and annual rewards distribution. Customers will first register by  
  providing their residence address, telephone number, and driving license number, after  
  which the system assigns them a unique Customer Number (CN). Each time a  
  purchase is made, the customer presents their CN, and the system records the purchase  
  value against the CN. The total purchase value is tracked throughout the year for each  
  customer. At the end of the year, the system selects the top 10 customers with the      (5)  
  highest purchase totals and awards them surprise gifts. Additionally, any customer  
  whose purchases exceed Rs. 10,000 is awarded a 22-carat gold coin. After the year-end  
  rewards are distributed, all customer purchase records are reset for the new year,  
  ensuring a fresh start. The software system will maintain customer details, track  
  purchase amounts, and generate the lists of top customers and gold coin awardees at the  
  end of each year. The Data Dictionary will include items such as customer details,  
  unique CNs, purchase amounts, total purchases, top customer lists, and gold coin award  
  eligibility. The system ensures accurate purchase tracking, automatic rewards  
  generation, and timely record resets, making the scheme efficient and effective in  
  encouraging customer loyalty.  
  
  4A)   Design and draw use case diagram for hospital management system which manages  
  appointments, patient records, billing and inventory.                                      (3)  
  
  4B)   Design and draw UML sequence diagram for a food delivery service that allows  
  customers to place orders, which are then sent to restaurants and tracked for delivery.    (5)  
  
  4C)   Design and draw UML state chart diagram for library management system that models  
  the lifecycle of a book from availability to being borrowed and returned.                  (2)  
  
  5A)   List the key difference between Black-box and White box testing using suitable  
  examples.                                                                                  (2)
